root.label: New York Times/Siena October 2026 five-state Senate poll

events.label: New York Times/Siena October 2026 five-state Senate poll

slots.name: Peltola poll share
slots.sentence: The Times/Siena poll found Democrat Mary Peltola, a former member of Congress, held a seven-point lead over incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska.

slots.name: Talarico poll share
slots.sentence: In Texas, Democrat James Talarico had a six-point lead (51% to 45%) over Republican Ken Paxton, according to the poll, conducted Sept. 21-Oct. 1.

slots.name: Brown poll margin
slots.sentence: Also in the poll, former U.S. senator Sherrod Brown had a three-point margin in Ohio over Sen. Jon Husted, who was appointed to fill the empty seat left when JD Vance became vice president.

slots.name: Kansas election gap
slots.sentence: In Kansas, where it has been more than 90 years since a Democrat was elected to the U.S. Senate, Methodist pastor Adam Hamilton is tied with Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, the poll found.

slots.name: Iowa election gap
slots.sentence: Similarly, Democrats have not won a Senate race in 18 years in Iowa where Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek trails Republican U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson by one percentage point.

slots.name: Alaska poll result
slots.sentence: - Alaska: (D) Peltola: 50% - (R) Sullivan: 43%

slots.name: Iowa poll result
slots.sentence: - Iowa: (R) Hinson: 48% - (D) Turek: 47%

slots.name: Kansas poll result
slots.sentence: - Kansas: (D) Hamilton: 45% - (R) Marshall: 45%

slots.name: Ohio poll result
slots.sentence: - Ohio: (D) Brown: 49% - (R) Husted: 46%

slots.name: Texas poll result
slots.sentence: - Texas: (D) Talarico: 51% - (R) Paxton: 45%

slots.name: Trump disapproval share
slots.sentence: The poll also found that 57% of those surveyed across the five states strongly or somewhat disapproved of Trump's job as president – just the latest sign of disapproval of the president's performance.

slots.name: Economy issue share
slots.sentence: More than one-fifth of likely voters (21%) said the economy was the most important issue in deciding their vote.

slots.name: Other issue share
slots.sentence: Other important issues: inflation/cost of living (8%), character/competence of candidate (8%) and Immigration (8%).

slots.name: Seats needed
slots.sentence: Democrats need to gain at least four seats currently held by Republicans while also holding onto their current Senate seats to assume control.

slots.name: Senate party count
slots.sentence: The Senate has 53 Republicans and 47 Democrats including two Independents (Sen. Angus Young of Maine and Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont), who caucus with them.

slots.name: Competitive state count
slots.sentence: Democrats are also competitive in five other states Trump won by double digits in 2024: Florida, Nebraska, Mississippi, South Carolina and Kentucky.

slots.name: MAGA spending pledge
slots.sentence: Through his MAGA political action committee, Trump has pledged to spend $400 million to boost Republicans in the midterms.

slots.name: Texas spending
slots.sentence: At the same time, the Senate Leadership Fund is spending $100 million in Texas to bolster Paxton in what has become an unexpectedly competitive state.

slots.name: release date
slots.sentence: A new New York Times/Siena University poll, released Oct. 2, found Democrats has leads or were neck and neck in key Senate races in five states – Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio and Texas – considered to be reliably Republican.

slots.name: fieldwork dates
slots.sentence: conducted Sept. 21-Oct. 1
